To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the framing of climate change as an issue of responsibilities and rights has become more prominent in recent times, (ii) the framing of responsibilities and rights within the context of climate change is not a neutral process and has implications for the way in which the politics of climate change is understood and addressed, and (iii) the framing of responsibility and rights within climate change politics has implications for the politics of climate governance and the ways in which the issue of climate change will be addressed in the future

climate change governance is currently caught in a number of governance traps that are structural in nature, and that the ways in which the concepts of rights and responsibilities are framed in climate change politics are central to the dynamics through which these traps arise.

The governance traps in climate change policy arise from the framing of the problem in terms of responsibilities, rather than rights, which has led to an overemphasis on agency and a neglect of the structural conditions which give rise to these governance traps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the politics of climate change and how it is understood in the policy community.
the question of why the climate change issue has been such a difficult one to address.
the ways in which climate change is framed within the political process, in particular how the attribution of agency is structured.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the climate change is the most important issue in the 21st century.
the climate is changing and the human activity is the main reason for this change.

The Paris Agreement is an important first step towards a global response to climate change that can limit warming to well below 2°C, and is the first global climate agreement to include a long-term goal on adaptation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current governance system of climate change is a trap.
climate change is a global issue that requires global governance.
we are concerned about the ways in which the politics of climate change are being framed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way in which the problems of climate change are framed is important.
we need to be more attentive to how the framing of agency in climate politics has become a governance trap.

climate change is a problem of governance, not just of policy, and that the way we understand the problem and the way we attribute agency in relation to it are critical in determining how the problem is addressed.
